name: Refuse.dev
title: A second thought before the install.
description: An open-source security layer for the packages developers, agents and CI want to install.
problem: Agents can move from a suggestion to a package installation quickly. That makes the installation step a useful place to check known vulnerabilities before a dependency becomes part of a project.
approach: Refuse combines a package-manager shim with a checking server. The CLI intercepts installation requests, asks the server to evaluate a package version and refuses known-vulnerable versions with a safer-version suggestion. The same idea applies to a developer’s shell, an agent and CI.
details: A CLI layer wraps package managers so checks sit in the existing install workflow.
The server can be self-hosted; the project also offers a hosted backend.
MCP integration connects the checks to agent tooling.
contribute: Explore the server and CLI repositories, reproduce an issue, or propose a focused improvement. The repositories include the current contribution and security guidance.

name: slm.expert
title: A smaller model. A better fit.
description: A discovery resource for small open-weight models, organized around the job you need them to do.
problem: Model discovery becomes difficult when a single leaderboard stands in for every task. Function calling, extraction, document understanding and classification ask different things of a model.
approach: slm.expert organizes small open-weight models by use case. Model pages bring together published benchmark results, licenses and platform information, with links back to the evidence. It gives builders a place to narrow their options before testing in their own workflow.
details: Task-oriented categories cover areas such as tool use, structured extraction and document AI.
Published scores are presented with their sources so comparisons can be checked.
License information is part of the model decision, alongside capability and size.
contribute: Explore the directory and bring corrections, missing models or useful evidence into the conversation. This is a resource about open-weight models; each model’s own license still applies.

name: Agentend.ai
title: From an intent to a working backend.
description: An open-source framework that organizes agent-powered backends around capabilities, memory, workers and events.
problem: An agent-powered product needs more than a model call. It needs a way to route intent, supply context, coordinate work and deliver results back to the interface.
approach: Agentend explores a capability-oriented backend. A kernel routes intent, a context bus supplies memory, workers carry out tasks and events stream to the frontend. This makes agent behavior part of the application architecture.
details: Capabilities give the application a domain-focused unit of behavior.
Workers and orchestration structure how a task moves through the system.
The project documents AG-UI, MCP and A2A integrations, along with observability.
contribute: Read the architecture, explore an example and use the repository to discuss a change or submit a contribution. Check the project’s license and contribution guidance before building on it.
